skim: Typhoon Dujuan’s Japan death toll rose to nine with four still missing, while Morocco’s PAM party won a fractious election on turnout of just 38%, its second-lowest since 2002.
Iran called Trump’s UN threat to “annihilate” it “strategic desperation” and warned of a “crushing” response, as Trump’s Board of Peace unveiled a $2.45 billion first-phase Gaza rebuilding plan.
Trump hosted Xi Jinping in Washington for their first meeting in the US capital in 11 years, even as Wall Street sold off on a jump in Treasury yields to their highest since 2007.

Anthropic said its Claude AI autonomously discovered a novel CRISPR-like gene-editing enzyme system after a 21-hour, 950-agent research run, rattling gene-editing stocks the same week it cut its own Opus pricing 20%.

Cyclone Arnab made landfall on India’s east coast overnight, Saudi Arabia’s strikes on Houthi targets have reportedly killed over 150 people in two days, and Qatar’s Amir drew praise from envoys in Doha for his UN mediation address.

stories.headline: Typhoon Dujuan’s Japan Death Toll Climbs to Nine as Search for Missing Continues
stories.body: The confirmed death toll from Typhoon Dujuan in eastern Japan rose to nine on Thursday — six in Chiba Prefecture, three in Kanagawa — with four more people still unaccounted for, per The Nation (Sep 24). Rescue teams recovered a woman’s body in Kanagawa and pulled a man from a submerged vehicle in Chiba, a region already battered by flooding earlier this summer.

stories.headline: Morocco’s PAM Wins Parliamentary Election as Turnout Sinks to 38%
stories.body: Morocco’s Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM) topped Wednesday’s parliamentary election with 97 of 395 seats, ahead of the RNI (66) and Istiqlal (65), the interior minister said in preliminary results, per ThePrint (Sep 24). Turnout came in at just 38.02%, Morocco’s second-lowest since 2002 and well below 2021’s roughly 50% showing, raising fresh questions about the vote’s credibility, per Hespress (Sep 24).

stories.headline: Bangladesh Measles Toll Passes 1,076 as 11 Children Die in a Single Day
stories.body: Bangladesh’s measles outbreak claimed 11 more lives in the 24 hours to September 23, pushing the death toll to 1,076 — 101 of them laboratory-confirmed, the rest suspected — per The Business Standard (Sep 23). The country has logged 183,449 suspected cases and 162,048 hospitalizations since mid-March, according to Directorate General of Health Services data, with 1,157 fresh suspected cases reported in that same 24-hour window.

stories.headline: Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli Return as India Name ODI Squad for West Indies Series
stories.body: India have recalled Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli to the ODI squad, with Ravindra Jadeja also returning to 50-over cricket after being left out since the New Zealand series earlier this year, while Shubman Gill continues as captain, per Times of India/Yahoo Sports (Sep 23). The squad assembles in Thiruvananthapuram by Thursday ahead of the first of three ODIs against West Indies on Sep 27, with several first-choice players — Shreyas Iyer, Jasprit Bumrah and Axar Patel among them — still on Asian Games duty in Japan.

stories.headline: Afghanistan Crush Japan by 48 Runs in Asian Games Men’s Cricket Opener
stories.body: Arab Gul Momand took 4 for 8 and Nangeyalia Kharoti added 3 for 19 as Afghanistan bowled out Japan for 81 after posting 129 for 6, winning by 48 runs in the men’s cricket competition’s Group A opener at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin, per The SportsTak (Sep 24). Mohammad Akram top-scored with 34 off 29 balls for Afghanistan, who share Group A with Japan and Nepal — a separate tournament from the women’s event India won gold in earlier this week.

stories.headline: Verstappen Chases Back-to-Back Baku Win as F1 Race Moves to Saturday
stories.body: This weekend’s Azerbaijan Grand Prix has been shifted a day earlier — practice Thursday, qualifying Friday, race Saturday — to avoid clashing with Azerbaijan’s Remembrance Day on Sep 27, per Formula1.com (Sep 21). Max Verstappen, tied with Sergio Pérez for most Baku wins after a pole-to-flag ‘grand slam’ there in 2025, could become the first driver to win back-to-back races at the circuit, though Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar remains a doubt after a wrist injury with Liam Lawson continuing to deputize.

stories.headline: Barcelona Femení Reach 900 Career Wins With Rout of Paris FC
stories.body: Barcelona’s women’s team beat Paris FC 5-2 in their Women’s Champions League opener, with Ewa Pajor scoring twice, to register the club’s 900th official victory since 1988 — a win rate above 72% across 1,247 matches — per Goal.com (Sep 23). Kerolin, Clara Serrajordi and Caroline Graham also scored as Barcelona opened their continental title defense in style.

stories.headline: Chelsea Survive Austria Wien Scare to Open Women’s Champions League Campaign
stories.body: Wieke Kaptein’s 11th-minute strike, which deflected in off the crossbar, was enough for Chelsea to beat debutants Austria Wien 1-0 in their Women’s Champions League opener, per beIN Sports (Sep 23). Manager Sonia Bompastor said her side needs to be more clinical after Austria Wien — roused by Modesta Uka — created several second-half chances to equalize.

stories.headline: Trump Hosts Xi in Washington for First DC Summit in 11 Years
stories.body: President Trump welcomed Chinese leader Xi Jinping to Washington on Wednesday for their first meeting in the U.S. capital in 11 years, with trade, rare earths, Taiwan, Iran and AI on the agenda, per OPB (Sep 23). China is expected to announce fresh purchases of American agricultural goods while Washington weighs tariff cuts on consumer goods such as footwear and apparel, though a rare-earths truce extension remained unresolved as talks continued.

stories.headline: Stocks Slide as Treasury Yields Hit Highest Since 2007
stories.body: Tuesday’s Nasdaq record reversed Wednesday as the Dow fell about 0.6–0.7%, the S&P 500 dropped roughly 0.8% and the Nasdaq slid about 1.1%, per TheStreet (Sep 23). The sell-off followed a stronger-than-expected S&P Global composite PMI reading of 58.4 that pushed the 10-year Treasury yield to 5.11% and the 5-year above 5% for the first time since 2007, fueling bets on further Fed tightening; Fed Governor Michael Barr said “further policy adjustments are likely to be needed to ensure inflation comes down to target in a timely fashion.”

stories.headline: Oil Extends Slide as Brent Drops Below $96 on Iran Diplomacy
stories.body: Brent crude fell under $96 a barrel, down nearly 10% over five trading days, as hopes for easing U.S.-Iran tensions grew after the two countries held hours of talks at the United Nations, per Yahoo Finance (Sep 23). Gold, by contrast, held in the $4,300–$4,394-an-ounce range as investors weighed the diplomatic thaw against the Trump-Xi summit getting underway in Washington the same day.

stories.headline: AT&T Says It Won’t Backfill Jobs Lost to AI and Fiber Automation
stories.body: AT&T said it does not expect to maintain its current headcount as AI-driven automation and its shift from copper to fiber networks cut truck rolls and manual technician work, per TechStartups and Cryptobriefing (both Sep 23). The carrier has cut roughly 10,000 jobs since 2025 — 8,000 last year and 2,100 in the first half of 2026, leaving about 131,000 employees as of June — and is targeting $4 billion in annual savings by 2028, though it rejected a reported 85,000-worker cut target as inaccurate.

stories.headline: Anthropic Says Claude Autonomously Discovered a Novel CRISPR-Like Enzyme System
stories.body: Anthropic said its Claude AI model, working with roughly 950 agents over about 21 hours, identified a previously uncharacterized three-part enzyme system, dubbed “ART,” in giant bacteriophage DNA that resembles CRISPR’s cut-copy-paste targeting machinery, though its actual editing function remains unproven, per TechCrunch (Sep 23). CRISPR pioneer Feng Zhang of MIT called the finding “genuinely intriguing” and worth further investigation, while Anthropic noted a Stanford team had previously identified a broadly similar system.

stories.headline: Anthropic Cuts Opus Pricing 20% With Claude Opus 5.5
stories.body: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5, cutting output-token pricing to $20 per million tokens from $25 and matching the larger Fable model’s performance on many benchmarks while running faster, per TechCrunch (Sep 22). Anthropic called it “the strongest-performing model we’ve tested to date,” with Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 versions planned “in the coming weeks” as the AI pricing war that saw OpenAI and xAI slash rates this week now reaches Anthropic’s flagship line.

stories.headline: Microsoft Dismantles AI-Powered EvilTokens Phishing Ring
stories.body: Microsoft and UK police took down EvilTokens, an AI-powered phishing-as-a-service platform that compromised more than 12,000 inboxes across 10,000-plus organizations by exploiting Microsoft’s OAuth device-code login flow, per The Hacker News (Sep 22). Two men, aged 32 and 38, were arrested September 11; SpyCloud’s Trevor Hilligoss said the AI tooling meant the manual parts of business email compromise “used to require human involvement” and were now “available to anyone for $500 a month.”

stories.headline: Hackers Claim Breach of FBI Employee and Applicant Data
stories.body: Extortion group ShinyHunters claimed it stole terabytes of data from the FBI, including names, addresses and phone numbers of agents and their spouses plus job-applicant records from FBIjobs.gov, accessed via a breached Oracle PeopleSoft server, per TechCrunch (Sep 22). The FBI said it is “aware of claims regarding unauthorized activity affecting FBIjobs.gov and is currently investigating,” marking the bureau’s second known system breach this year.

stories.headline: Qualcomm Debuts First 2nm Mobile Chips With 5GHz Cores
stories.body: Qualcomm unveiled the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and Elite Extreme Gen 6, its first chips built on TSMC’s 2nm process and the first mobile processors to hit 5GHz CPU speeds, per Tech Times (Sep 23). The Extreme variant supports on-device mixture-of-experts AI models above 30 billion parameters and pairs LPDDR6 memory with a Hexagon NPU boasting 35% more performance, positioning the chips as the hardware backbone for on-phone AI agents.

stories.headline: Iran Calls Trump’s “Annihilate” Threat “Strategic Desperation,” Warns of Crushing Response
stories.body: Iran’s military dismissed President Trump’s UN threat to “annihilate” Iran as a sign of Washington’s “strategic desperation,” warning it is prepared to launch “more crushing and less predictable” attacks if hostilities resume, per Dropsite News (Sep 23). At parallel UN talks, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei laid out three conditions to end the standoff — an end to U.S. “acts of aggression,” a halt to the naval blockade and economic warfare, and release of frozen Iranian assets — stressing “this was not anything new” in Iran’s position.

stories.headline: Trump’s Board of Peace Unveils $2.45 Billion Blueprint for Gaza Reconstruction
stories.body: Trump’s Board of Peace proposed a six-month, $2.45 billion plan covering 66 projects in infrastructure, education and health, a first step toward an estimated $35.2 billion medium-term and $71.4 billion ten-year rebuild, per CP24/AP (Sep 23). Board high representative Nikolay Mladenov called the need “immense,” acknowledging “enormous hurdles that must still be overcome” as Hamas disarmament remains incomplete and no international peacekeeping force has yet deployed since the October 10 ceasefire.

stories.headline: Zelensky Offers Russia an Energy Truce After Trump Meeting
stories.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Kyiv is “ready for energy ceasefire,” adding “if they don’t want us to attack their diesel and refineries…we are ready — if they will not attack our energy system,” per Al Jazeera (Sep 23). No deal was reached to unilaterally halt Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries; Trump, who met Zelensky on the sidelines of UNGA, said the attacks were pushing up global diesel prices and that a resolution was coming, adding “I think it’s going to happen.”

stories.headline: Nauru Becomes Sixth Nation to Announce ICC Withdrawal Since Trump’s UNGA Call
stories.body: Nauru President David Adeang told the UN General Assembly the ICC “has lost its relevance” to his country and that he would file withdrawal papers with the Rome Statute depositary before leaving New York, per TASS (Sep 23). The move follows Trump’s UNGA appeal for “all nations” to quit what he called a “rogue” court, and makes Nauru the sixth state to announce an ICC exit, joining Venezuela, Chad, Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger.

fixtures.headline: Irani Cup Opens Domestic Season in Srinagar
fixtures.body: Ranji Trophy champions Jammu & Kashmir host a Rest of India side captained by Rishabh Pant in the four-day Irani Cup at the Sher-e-Kashmir Stadium, Srinagar, Oct 1–5.

fixtures.headline: Azerbaijan GP Race Day Moves to Saturday in Baku
fixtures.body: Practice runs Thursday and qualifying Friday, with the race itself brought forward to Saturday, Sep 25–27, so it doesn’t clash with Azerbaijan’s Remembrance Day on the 27th.

fixtures.headline: India-West Indies T20I Series Begins in Lucknow
fixtures.body: After the ODIs, Shreyas Iyer’s India open a five-match T20I series against West Indies in Lucknow on Oct 6, with further games in Ranchi, Indore, Hyderabad and Bengaluru through Oct 17, per BCCI (Sep 16).

portfolio.headline: Gene-Editing Stocks Rattled as Anthropic’s Claude Uncovers CRISPR-Like System
portfolio.body: CRISPR Therapeutics was among the gene-editing developers pressured after Anthropic disclosed that Claude uncovered a novel three-component enzyme system resembling CRISPR’s targeting mechanism in bacteriophage DNA during a roughly 21-hour automated research run. The finding raised questions about whether AI-driven discovery could eventually surface new gene-editing tools outside the intellectual-property positions held by incumbents, though scientists including MIT’s Feng Zhang cautioned the system’s real-world editing function is still unproven. Per TechCrunch (Sep 23).

portfolio.headline: CrowdStrike Wins Gartner ‘Customers’ Choice’ as Wall Street Hikes AI-Security Targets
portfolio.body: CrowdStrike was named the sole Customers’ Choice in Gartner’s 2026 Identity Threat Detection report, and disclosed that Falcon Identity annual recurring revenue grew 34% year-over-year to exceed $585 million. Morgan Stanley, Stephens, Wedbush and BofA all raised price targets this week — Stephens to $280 and Morgan Stanley to $254 — calling CrowdStrike a “prime winner” of rising AI-security spending, while the company also expanded its Project QuiltWorks integrations with OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia and AWS and launched a CISO Command Center with Wipro. Per StocksToTrade (Sep 23).

portfolio.headline: Alphabet Faces AI Pricing War as OpenAI and Anthropic Slash Model Costs
portfolio.body: Alphabet came under pressure after OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and Luna with prices cut roughly 50%, and Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5.5 at about 20% lower cost than its predecessor, raising concern that cheaper rival models could compress Google Cloud’s inference margins just as Alphabet raised its 2026 capital-expenditure forecast to $195-205 billion. Sentiment was further weighed down by Meta’s Muse AI assistant, which topped 2.8 million downloads in its first 12 days ahead of Meta’s Connect conference. Per Yahoo Finance (Sep 23).

portfolio.headline: Palantir Loses $875 Million FAA Contract to Rival but Keeps Government Foothold
portfolio.body: The FAA awarded a 12-year, $875 million contract for its Flow Management Data and Services platform and SMART air-traffic system to rival Air Space Intelligence instead of Palantir. The agency nonetheless said Palantir remains the only vendor able to plug into its existing systems without major new development, and Rosenblatt analyst John McPeake reiterated a Buy rating and $225 price target, noting Palantir’s U.S. government revenue grew 90% year-over-year to $809 million in the second quarter. Per Benzinga (Sep 23).

portfolio.headline: Oracle Lands Co-op Live Arena Deal as Broader Tech Selloff Weighs on Shares
portfolio.body: Oracle announced that Co-op Live, the UK’s largest indoor arena, is deploying Oracle Simphony Cloud Point of Sale and Oracle NetSuite to run its food-and-beverage operations, extending Oracle’s push into hospitality and live-entertainment cloud contracts. The news came alongside a broader technology-sector pullback that weighed on megacap tech names generally; Wall Street’s consensus price target on Oracle remains near $250, though several analysts have trimmed individual targets into the $200-225 range. Per Benzinga (Sep 23).

portfolio.headline: Coeur Mining Slips as Silver Retreats on Stronger Dollar and Hawkish Fed Talk
portfolio.body: Silver prices pulled back on Sep 23 as a firmer U.S. dollar and hawkish Federal Reserve commentary on “persistent inflation risks” pushed Treasury yields higher, denting demand for non-yielding precious metals. The retreat came after silver failed to clear resistance at the top of its recent multi-week trading range, triggering technical profit-taking, while easing Middle East tensions from U.S.-Iran talks also reduced safe-haven flows; long-term industrial demand from solar, automotive and electronics remained intact even as near-term price action stayed macro-driven. Per TradingKey (Sep 23).

portfolio.headline: Editas Medicine Slides Alongside Sector After Anthropic’s CRISPR-Like AI Discovery
portfolio.body: Editas Medicine was also among the gene-editing developers pressured after Anthropic’s disclosure, as investors weighed whether AI-driven biological discovery could reshape the competitive landscape for gene-editing intellectual property over time. MIT’s Feng Zhang, a CRISPR pioneer, said the newly identified enzyme system was “genuinely intriguing” but cautioned its real-world editing function remains unproven and would need substantial further validation. Per TechCrunch (Sep 23).

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab Makes Landfall, Over 5,000 Evacuated Across Odisha
stories.body: Cyclone Arnab’s crossing was underway late Wednesday between Kalingapatnam and Visakhapatnam–Gopalpur, with more than 5,000 people relocated to cyclone shelters in Odisha, including pregnant women and the elderly, per ETV Bharat (Sep 23). Twenty-eight fishing boats sheltered at Paradip Port as heavy rain and rough seas battered the coast; Malkangiri Collector Prathamesh Arvind Rajeshirke said authorities were aiming for “zero casualties.”

stories.headline: India Rejects Erdogan’s Kashmir Remarks as ‘Unwarranted and Unacceptable’
stories.body: After Turkish President Erdogan again raised Kashmir at the UNGA, calling for the dispute to be resolved “through dialogue within the framework of the United Nations Charter,” India’s external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal called the remarks “unwarranted and unacceptable” interference and lodged a formal protest with Turkey’s ambassador in New Delhi, per WION (Sep 22). MEA reiterated that “Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of India.”

stories.headline: Banks Set for Five-Day Shutdown as Unions Confirm September 28–30 Strike
stories.body: SBI and Union Bank customers face a five-day service gap after the United Forum of Bank Unions’ confirmed three-day strike (Sep 28–30) runs into the weekend, per WION (Sep 22). Nine unions are pressing for a five-day workweek and withdrawal of the Performance Linked Incentive scheme; SBI has urged customers to finish essential transactions early and rely on ATMs, UPI and net banking.

stories.headline: Burnham Tells UN Israeli Settlements Threaten Two-State Solution
stories.body: PM Andy Burnham warned the UN General Assembly that “if we fail to back those words with deeds, we will further corrode trust in the political, diplomatic and international process,” specifically condemning Israel’s E1 settlement project as a plan that “would drive a wedge through the West Bank,” per Al Jazeera (Sep 23). London has already banned trade in goods from illegal West Bank settlements; Canada and France issued parallel statements the same day.

stories.headline: Burnham Pitches ‘Time for Britain to Believe Again’ Ahead of Labour Conference
stories.body: Previewing this weekend’s Labour Party conference in Liverpool, Burnham said “the message will be it’s time for Britain to believe again, it’s time for Britain to have hope again,” per Express & Star (Sep 23). The conference is expected to center on October’s Budget and a promised 10-year national plan, with possible friction from Labour’s left over the government’s Gaza policy.

stories.headline: World Envoys in Doha Praise Amir’s UN Address on Regional Mediation
stories.body: Diplomats in Doha welcomed Amir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al-Thani’s UNGA address, per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 23). Turkish Ambassador Yakup Caymazoğlu called mediation “a strategic foreign policy instrument,” while British Ambassador Neerav Patel said Qatar “has become an important voice for dialogue and diplomacy, and a valued partner in efforts to promote regional stability.”

stories.headline: Saudi Strikes on Houthi Targets Kill Scores, Yemen Displacement Nears 230,000
stories.body: Saudi Arabia’s promised “sizeable response” has materialized: strikes on Houthi positions have left between roughly 118 and 154 people dead over two days by competing tallies, including six civilians in Mocha, per Courthouse News (Sep 22). The UN forecasts Yemen displacement could climb from over 130,000 toward 230,000; King Salman called an alleged Houthi threat against Mecca “a provocation to Muslims around the world.”

stories.headline: Trump Meets GCC Leaders in New York Amid Fears of Wider Iran War
stories.body: Trump met leaders from Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and other Gulf states on the UNGA sidelines as the seven-month US-Israel war on Iran continues to disrupt Gulf energy exports, per Al Jazeera (Sep 22). Analyst Giorgio Cafiero of Gulf State Analytics said the Gulf states “will probably seek to underscore their own vulnerabilities to a renewed cycle of all-out fighting,” while Qatar pushes to protect gas exports and Saudi Arabia presses Washington on the Houthis.

doha_events.headline: Sid Sriram Brings South Indian, Hindi Hits to QNCC
doha_events.body: Chennai-based playback singer Sid Sriram performs live at Qatar National Convention Centre’s Hall 7 on September 25, spanning his South Indian and Hindi film catalogue. Tickets start at QR220 via Platinumlist.

doha_events.headline: Mena W Fena Pop-Up Spotlights Local Makers at Al Hazm Mall
doha_events.body: An open-air market in Al Hazm Mall’s outdoor courtyard opens today, September 24, running daily 3pm–11pm into late October and showcasing local artisans’ handcrafted fashion, accessories and home décor, per Qatar Living’s weekly roundup (Sep 23).

doha_events.headline: Comedian John Achkar Debuts Arabic Special ‘Feena Nehke?’ in Doha
doha_events.body: Stand-up comic John Achkar brings his most personal Arabic show yet to Abdul Aziz Nasser Theatre on September 25–26, tackling identity, family and faith with the raw, observational style that has sold over 150,000 tickets across his prior specials. Tickets from QR195; 13+ with a content advisory.

doha_events.headline: 3-2-1 Museum Hosts Free Arabian Gulf Cup Screenings Through October 6
doha_events.body: The 3-2-1 Qatar Olympic and Sports Museum is screening every Arabian Gulf Cup match free with no registration required, per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 22). Qatar plays Bahrain on September 24 (9pm) and Yemen on September 27 (6:55pm), with the tournament running through an October 6 final.
